title: Syro-Malabar book states, editorial changes and restoration reception

traditions.label: Syro-Malabar Eucharistic books
traditions.scope: Syro-Malabar Syriac and approved operative Malayalam Eucharistic service-book language, with Latin restoration instruments and bounded reception; independent diaspora and lay translation histories are deferred.
traditions.coverage_note: 1774/1775 complementary books, a named 1845 exemplar, 1906 and 1946 editorial states, and the 1955–1962 restoration are distinguished. No continuous textual stemma is claimed.

sources.title: Ordo chaldaicus rituum et lectionum, Puttenpalli 1906
sources.inspection: Reopened full-size original physical PDF 508 (1904 permission) and 6 (1905 approval and 1906 imprint); title PDF 510 inspected in prior acquisition. Added section 55*–101* = whole PDF 69–23 identified, distinct from earlier appendix 1*–54*. Opening native headings PDF 69–67 and approval PDF 22 independently read on 2026-10-17; first entries Francis Xavier, Nicholas, Ambrose, Holy House and Lucy.
sources.limitations: Complete original scan held and registered; Syriac body and specific newly appended Masses not collated. Bonn physical page order is reversed for this RTL book.

sources.title: Matthaeus Vadakel, Ordo chaldaicus rituum et lectionum, Alwaye 1946: preliminary leaves

sources.title: Order of the Mysteries, Editio Typica, Rome 2003: title leaves

sources.title: Syro Malabar Taksa (Syriac) 2003 Editio Typica, black-and-white scan, Internet Archive item taksa2003bwsuriyani

stages.label: First Roman printed ordinary and lection collection
stages.scope: Complementary Eucharistic volumes; the sacramental ritual is excluded.
stages.witness_label: Ordo Chaldaicus Missae Beatorum Apostolorum (1774); Ordo Chaldaicus rituum et lectionum (1775)
stages.summary: The official retrospective reports received Maronite prayers, Latin-derived vesting and Holy Week material, and altered calendar/readings.

evidence.claim: Lists separate 1774 ordinary, 1775 sacramental ritual and 1775 rites-and-lections titles.
Describes prayer, ritual and calendar additions associated with the first printed Taksa.

evidence.locus: Praefatio Commissionis Liturgicae, printed v (PDF 3), second paragraph
evidence.claim: The 1960 Roman liturgical commission states that in the Missal edited at Rome in 1774 nothing appears besides the Apostles' anaphora except Epistles and Gospels taken from the Roman Missal and arranged by its calendar.

stages.limitations: No original 1774/1775 page comparison. The two Eucharistic books are not two successive revisions. The retrospective does not securely assign every item to an individual volume. The 1960 commission's description of the 1774 edition's proper is a retrospective that does not distinguish the 1774 ordinary from the 1775 lessons volume.
stages.reception: Prepared for Malabar Catholic worship; no claim that every reported addition originated in 1774.

stages.label: Propaganda exemplar named as 1845
stages.scope: Bounded earlier arrangement and absence of the later-approved appended Masses, as described in the 1904/1905 permissions.
stages.witness_label: Missale Syro-Chaldaeo-Malabaricum, Propaganda printing dated 1845 by the 1904 permission
stages.summary: The permission describes an exemplar with dispersed ordinary material and Rogation readings in a supplement.

evidence.claim: Explicitly names Propaganda printings of 1775 and 1845 and describes the earlier arrangement.
Calls the Masses approved on 31 July 1905 newly appended after comparison with the exemplar; only their prior absence is inferred.

stages.limitations: Propers scope is limited to the reported absence of the newly appended 1905 Masses, not a complete proper inventory. Documented as a named exemplar, not an independently identified physical edition or a proven substantive revision of 1775. Do not equate it with the separately reported 1844 lection book or 1845 sacramental ritual.
stages.reception: An authorized editorial exemplar for the 1906 Malabar book; its actual historical use is not reconstructed.

stages.label: Reorganized travel missal with appended Masses
stages.scope: Andreas Kalapura edition: arrangement and additions explicitly described in its permissions.
stages.witness_label: Ordo chaldaicus rituum et lectionum, Puttenpalli, Mar Thoma Sliha Press, 1906
stages.summary: Collects the ordinary, moves the three pre-Septuagesima Rogation readings into place, and adds the 1905-authorized Masses in a distinct 55*–101* section, beginning with December feasts.

evidence.claim: Directs collection of the ordinary and relocation of Rogation readings.

evidence.locus: Physical PDF 6, 15 October 1905 approval and 1906 imprint
evidence.claim: Reports comparison with the exemplar and newly appended Masses approved by the Congregation of Rites on 31 July 1905.
The reproduced 10 August 1905 official reply reports the Rites 31 July nulla osta for the requested insertion.
Opening native entries identify Francis Xavier (3 December), Nicholas (6 December), Ambrose (7 December), Holy House (10 December) and Lucy (13 December).

Running heads of PDF 68–23 (printed 56*–101*) read on 2026-10-21: the section is titled throughout as added feasts (ʿeʾdē mawsfē) arranged by month — Kanun I/December 55*–56*, Kanun II/January 57*–58*, Shbat/February 59*–64*, Adar/March 65*–67*, Nisan/April 68*–69*, Iyar/May 70*–71*, a Sacred Heart of our Lord feast 72*, Haziran/June 73*–76*, a second feast headed 'of the Heart' 77*, Tammuz/July 78*–81*, Ab/August 82*–83*, a separately headed feast 84*, Elul/September 85* and 87* with the Holy Name of Mary 86*, Teshri I/October 88*–93*, Teshri II/November 94*–97*, and a separately headed closing block 98*–101*.

stages.limitations: The added section's month-by-month structure and three separately headed feasts are read from running heads; individual entries inside each month block are not enumerated, the headers at 77*, 84* and 98*–101* are not securely read beyond their opening words, and no prayer body is transcribed. The older appendix 1*–54* is not attributed to the 1905 permission.
stages.reception: Aloysius Pareparambil petitioned also on behalf of the other two Syrian apostolic vicars. Propaganda’s reply reports the Rites nulla osta for insertion; the 15 October 1905 imprimatur authorizes printing. Neither record establishes universal actual adoption.

stages.label: Roman exemplar described by the 1946 editor
stages.scope: Only features explicitly contrasted by the 1946 foreword.
stages.witness_label: Unidentified Roman edition named in Augustine Kandathil’s foreword to Vadakel 1946
stages.summary: Prayers/rubrics were dispersed; some feasts appeared only in the calendar; server prayers were merely indicated; Marian Huthama was absent.

evidence.claim: Describes the edition against which Vadakel’s changes are stated.

stages.limitations: No date or exact Roman printing is named. This contextual state cannot be merged with the 1845 exemplar without further evidence.
stages.reception: Malabar liturgical exemplar, not the Latin Roman Missal; the phrase Roman Edition indicates printing context here.

stages.label: Vadakel’s corrected and expanded arrangement
stages.scope: Editorial arrangement and specified additions verified in original preliminary leaves.
stages.witness_label: Ordo Chaldaicus rituum et lectionum, reditus a P. Matthaeo Vadakel, Mar Thoma Sleeha, Alwaye, 1946
stages.summary: Regroups and brackets transferred material, supplies proper and server texts, and preserves a Nineveh appendix with Marian Huthama.

evidence.locus: Physical PDF 2–4, title, foreword and contents
evidence.claim: Dates the printing and explicitly describes the changed content and arrangement.
Names Holy See letter Prot. 2521/28 of 3 September 1930 for double-asterisk feasts and the Immaculate Conception Gospel.

stages.limitations: Bodies of the ordinary, propers and appendix are absent from the excerpt. No direct descent from the 1906 book is asserted. The 1930 act is reported in the book, not independently inspected.
stages.reception: Approved by Augustine Kandathil in the foreword dated 13 May 1946; catalogue’s 1945 date is not followed.

stages.label: Latin study text for restoration
stages.scope: Consultative formulation of the original reform, not a lay translation lineage.
stages.witness_label: Liturgia Siro-Malabaresi: Revisione e Ristampa del Messale Siro-Malabarese, Rome 1955, Prot. 947/48
stages.summary: Contains the common order, three anaphoras and forms of celebration for episcopal consultation.

evidence.claim: Identifies the Latin consultative text and its component page ranges.

stages.limitations: Book not acquired. Publication in 1955 is distinct from approval on 26 June 1957 and reception in 1962.
stages.reception: Roman commission study text; not asserted to have been used as a Latin-language altar missal.

stages.label: Restoration issued in complementary books
stages.scope: Rubrics/calendar, propers and a restricted Syriac ordinary issued separately.
stages.witness_label: Ordo celebrationis Quddasa (Rome 1959); Supplementum Mysteriorum (Rome 1960); Taksa d’Quddasa (Alwaye 1960)
stages.summary: The three books supply different components; the Syriac ordinary includes only Addai and Mari in the simple form.

evidence.claim: Distinguishes the approved three-anaphora programme, companion books, and narrower 12 May 1960 Syriac printing.
Lists the three books as publications of the restoration.

evidence.locus: PDF 138 Syriac title and 1960 Alwaye imprint; PDF 137 concordat and imprimatur dated 12 May 1960; PDF 136-75 printed 1-62
evidence.claim: The Syriac Taksa d-Quddasha printed at Alwaye in 1960, with Archbishop Joseph Parecattil's imprimatur of 12 May 1960, is present as a separately titled 62-page part of the 1962 book.

evidence.locus: PDF 1 title; PDF 2 imprimatur 5 January 1960; PDF 5 index
evidence.claim: The Latin proper volume, Prot. N. 947/48, Rome 1960, imprimatur 5 January 1960, has an index of Hudra items beginning on pp. 3-163 and Gazza items beginning on pp. 169-257 (start pages of entries, not part extents).

evidence.locus: Document 30, printed 207; Latin Appendix I, printed 387
evidence.claim: The 20 January 1962 instruction names the three books issued after the papal approval of 26 June 1957: the Syriac Taksa d-Quddasha with the ordinary and the anaphora of Addai and Mari, the Latin Ordo celebrationis Quddasa regulating three forms of celebration, and the Latin Supplementum Mysteriorum.

stages.limitations: The 1960 Syriac Taksa is now seen through its title, imprimatur and 62 pages as bound in the 1962 book, and the Supplementum through its title, imprimatur, preface and index; the Latin 1959 Ordo celebrationis is still unseen, and no body text is collated. The CMS file labelled 1959 is a 1998 translation. Companion volumes must not become sequential whole-missal revisions.
stages.reception: Programme approved by Pius XII in 1957; its complete contents were not all introduced in worship in 1962.

stages.label: Partial restoration introduced in worship
stages.scope: Community reception of the restricted restored order in the approved 1962 Syriac–Malayalam Qurbana book; its operative Malayalam text is received service-book language, while this stage remains limited to the partial restoration introduced in worship.
stages.witness_label: The Order of Qurbana of the Syro-Malabar Church, Alwaye 1962, Syriac and Malayalam
stages.summary: The bishops introduced the bilingual order on 3 July; several approved restored components remained unimplemented.

evidence.claim: Separates 20 January promulgation from 3 July introduction and identifies omitted components.

evidence.locus: RR-122/JT description, paragraphs on Syriac prayers and promulgation
evidence.claim: Identifies bilingual publication and continuing Syriac passages.

evidence.locus: PDF 7 title and 1962 Alwaye imprint; PDF 8 imprimatur of seven bishops, 3 July 1962; PDF 72 printed 58
evidence.claim: The bilingual book carries the seven bishops' imprimatur dated 3 July 1962; its Malayalam order ends at printed 58 and is followed by the separately titled 1960 Syriac Taksa.

evidence.locus: Document 30, printed 206-209; Appendix I, printed 387-389; narrative printed 197-198
evidence.claim: The Latin instruction of 20 January 1962 (Prot. 947/48) permits Malayalam in the entire Qurbana with anaphoras printed in Syriac and Malayalam, and sets transition norms; the bishops' joint pastoral letter of 18 June 1962 announced entry into force on 3 July 1962.

stages.limitations: A reception stage, not a new original-language revision inferred from translation. The 1962 instruction is read in a documentary edition's Latin text, not in the archival original; the bilingual book's Malayalam body is not collated.
stages.reception: Syro-Malabar episcopal introduction; not proof of uniform practice in every parish.

stages.label: 2003 Syriac typical-edition witness
stages.scope: Identified 2003 Syriac typical-edition printing whose order of Qurbana body (printed 12 to about 57) is now held; approval act, front matter and predecessor comparison unresolved.

stages.summary: Title identifies the Malabar use and Addai–Mari anaphora; native Syriac leaves are visible.

evidence.locus: Physical PDF 3–5, English/Syriac title leaves and first rubric leaf
evidence.claim: Confirms year, typical-edition designation and native Syriac content.

evidence.locus: PDF 1 Syriac title leaf; PDF 2 = printed 12; PDF 36 = printed 42; PDF 57 (number cut off; follows printed 56)
evidence.claim: A second copy reproduces the same Syriac title leaf and the Syriac order of Qurbana from printed 12 to its close at about printed 57, including a separately headed Order of the Fraction and Consignation at printed 42.

stages.limitations: Provisional because no approval decree, preface or changed-text statement has been found in either the CMS excerpt or the Internet Archive copy, and the body has not been collated against the 1960 Syriac Taksa (now held through the 1962 book) or the 1985/1989 orders. Do not count as an established substantive new stage from the title and body alone.
stages.reception: Title says use of the Church of the East Syrians of Malabar; Catholic bibliographic context corroborated by commission-hosted source list.
